intertext.note: root meeting
Possible: Yahweh calls Moshe's name out of the bush and tells him not to come closer. Thin: one shared verb and a mood.
The call from the Tent is answered on the eighth day: Moshe and Aharon go in, come out, and fire from Yahweh consumes the going up offering (9:22–24).
Elsewhere Moshe goes into the Tent and hears the voice from above the place of covering; here the voice comes out of the Tent to him.
Reception, possible: parastēsai, “to present,” bodies as a living sacrifice; may echo the bring-near language. Not checked against the Greek Old Testament.

typescenes.note: Tentative. The Tent in the mountain's place: cloud, Presence and a call (Exod 24:15–18; 40:34–35), zoned like Sinai. A variant: the Presence comes to the Tent and the call comes from it, with no entry.
